checks.name: SPF
checks.summary: 1 record, 5/10 DNS lookups, 0/2 void lookups, ends with ?all

findings.title: SPF ends with ?all
findings.explanation: '?all' (neutral) says nothing about servers not listed, so SPF gives no protection. End the record with '~all' or '-all'.

checks.name: DMARC
details: DKIM alignment adkim=r (relaxed: subdomains of the same organisational domain align)
SPF alignment aspf=r (relaxed: subdomains of the same organisational domain align)

findings.title: DMARC policy is p=none (monitoring only)
findings.explanation: p=none tells receivers to take no action on mail that fails DMARC: spoofed mail is still delivered normally. It is the right first stage while you read the aggregate reports, but it does not protect the domain. Staged path: (1) p=none with rua reports while you check that every legitimate sender passes SPF or DKIM with alignment; (2) p=quarantine (optionally with pct below 100 at first) so failing mail goes to spam; (3) p=reject once reports stay clean.

findings.title: No aggregate reports (rua)
findings.explanation: Without rua= you get no reports showing which servers send as your domain and whether they pass, so you cannot move safely to a stricter policy.

findings.title: Selector 'google': 1024-bit RSA key
findings.explanation: 1024-bit keys are still accepted but are the minimum; 2048 bits is the current recommendation. Rotate to a 2048-bit key (keep the old selector until mail signed with it has been delivered).
findings.record: google._domainkey.example.com. TXT "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=<new 2048-bit public key from your mail provider>"

findings.title: No MTA-STS record
findings.explanation: MTA-STS makes senders require TLS with a valid certificate when delivering to your MX hosts, blocking downgrade attacks. To enable it, serve a policy file as text/plain at https://mta-sts.example.com/.well-known/mta-sts.txt (valid HTTPS certificate for mta-sts.example.com) with mode: testing first, then publish the TXT record. Policy file: (one line each) version: STSv1 | mode: testing | mx: smtp.google.com | max_age: 604800

findings.title: No TLS-RPT record
findings.explanation: TLS-RPT asks senders to email you daily reports of TLS problems delivering to your domain; useful alongside MTA-STS.

checks.name: BIMI
details: BIMI shows your logo in some inboxes; it needs DMARC p=quarantine or p=reject and, for Gmail, a verified mark certificate.
